method: Same AI, separate pass after freezing. findings: The public page and registry identify the same Groningen bachelor. The public-facing programme page calls it European Languages, Cultures and Politics. The 2026–2027 regulations and catalogue use European Languages and Cultures. The example follows the September 2026 redesign, excluding transition entries. The neutral first-listed language and profile select German Plus and European Language and Society. It preserves 60 EC per year. The two chosen faculty-wide courses continue a theme of narrative and identity. The programme uses English or Dutch with academic work in the chosen major language. The chosen German course units are taught in German.

The route completes the 60 EC first year before Year 2. German Plus 1 precedes German Plus 2, which precedes German Plus 3 and each of the three German-specific first modules. The final interdisciplinary module follows German Plus 3 and at least two German-specific first modules. The ordinary 30 EC minor in the first half of Year 3 preserves open study space. An approved minor abroad is a genuine option with additional prerequisites. By the end of Year 2 the plan already has German Plus 3, Structure and Variation, Language Learning and all three first German-specific modules. This meets both the 35 EC specified by the regulations for the minor abroad and thesis and the detailed thesis entry rule. The normal route then takes the advanced German module, Research Methods, Language in the Mind and the 10 EC thesis. The thesis can also be undertaken in the major language through the corresponding course code.

The closest route directly responds to the language strand through beginner Dutch, stylistics and psycholinguistics and uses rhetorical analysis and applied communication for language in public life. Modern History and European Union Politics supply regional context. Introductory brain and behaviour precedes Psycholinguistics, which is only offered in the first spring. Qualitative methods move after introductory sociology and Rhetoric in Action moves to the final spring. The literature route has dedicated work in literary genres, theory, memoir, film and documentary. The description-only Renaissance Italy and Writing Art’s Histories strengthen its progression from close interpretation in a European setting to advanced inquiry about visual meaning and identity. The politics route preserves Modern History, comparative politics, European Union Politics and related sociology. The American Century seminar is complementary training in primary-source research rather than study of European political history. Media and identity courses drawing on American material supply comparative methods. Political philosophy, comparative politics, international relations and conflict anchor the distinct third option. The active workbook was searched for European languages, language instruction and progression in the named languages. Beginner Dutch and the study of linguistic structure, speech and bilingualism do not form a German or alternative European-language proficiency sequence. The comparison retains seven bounded pairings and leaves the specialist German modules, linguistic methods, minor and thesis unmatched.
